findings.claim: The notebook introduces a "composite risk feature" (risk_score) as an input feature for modeling.

findings.claim: "Stratified split BEFORE any transformation; preprocessing learns from the training set only."
findings.evidence: Although the split/preprocessing order in cell 8 is correct, cell 6 creates `risk_score` using `churned` on the full dataframe prior to the split. The narrative does not acknowledge this target-dependent feature engineering; no cell shows a version of `risk_score` built without using `churned`.

summary: Overall quality is not acceptable despite the notebook running cleanly and producing reproducible metrics. The most important issue is critical “target leakage”: the candidate creates an input feature using the true churn label, which artificially boosts performance and makes the test results invalid. There is also a major mismatch between what is written and what is actually computed (they claim AUC 0.99, but the executed test AUC is 0.858), which raises reliability concerns. In the interview, ask them to explain what target leakage is, identify why their risk_score is problematic, and describe how they would redesign the feature engineering and evaluation so the target is never used when building model inputs.
